advancement.solarpunk.biofuel_engine.des: Power a Biofuel Engine with the Biofuel you produced.
advancement.solarpunk.biomass.desc: Gather Biomass to start the biofuel production chain.
advancement.solarpunk.fermentation.desc: Produce Biofuel in a Fermentation Vat.
advancement.solarpunk.gasifier.desc: Ignite a Biomass Gasifier and put it to work.
advancement.solarpunk.geyser.desc: Cap a Geyser Vent for passive, round-the-clock geothermal power.
advancement.solarpunk.heat_battery.desc: Fill a Heat Battery with Molten Salt to store thermal energy.
advancement.solarpunk.root.desc: Collect Salt - the foundation of solar thermal energy.
advancement.solarpunk.solar_heater.desc: Craft a Solar Heater to begin concentrating sunlight into Molten Salt.
advancement.solarpunk.solar_tower.desc: Build a Solar Power Tower multiblock and bring it online.
advancement.solarpunk.steam_turbine.desc: Assemble a working Steam Turbine and generate rotational force from steam.
advancement.solarpunk.turbine_casing.des: Craft Turbine Casing - the structural blocks that form the Steam Turbine shell.
advancement.solarpunk.turbine_casing_gla: Craft Turbine Casing Glass to watch the blades spinning inside.
advancement.solarpunk.turbine_flooded.de: Let the condensate tank fill up and shut the turbine down. Pipe out the water next time.
block.solarpunk.andesite_solar_panel.too: 8-16 RPM with 1024-4096 SU of stress capacity. Stops in _rain_ and at _night_.
During the day with a clear sky
Generates _Rotational Force_ from sunlight. Output scales with sun angle and weather.
block.solarpunk.biofilter.tooltip.summar: Draws _Rotational Force_ to absorb _pollution_ from nearby chunks, gradually healing blocks and restoring biomes.
block.solarpunk.biofuel_engine.tooltip.b: Outputs 16 RPM with 8192 SU of stress capacity downward.
block.solarpunk.biofuel_engine.tooltip.s: Burns _Biofuel_ to generate _Rotational Force_. Pipe fuel into any face.
block.solarpunk.biomass_gasifier.tooltip: Outputs 8 RPM with 2048 SU of stress capacity downward.
Burns _Biomass_ to generate _Rotational Force_. Produces _Biochar_ as a byproduct.
block.solarpunk.brass_solar_panel.toolti: During the day with a clear sky
Generates _Forge Energy_ from sunlight. Output scales with sun angle and weather.
block.solarpunk.crystallizer.tooltip.beh: Pipe both input fluids in from any face; collect the result from the block or a hopper below, and any byproduct fluid from any face.
block.solarpunk.crystallizer.tooltip.sum: Runs data-driven recipes that turn up to two fluids into an item, plus an optional fluid byproduct. By default, quenches _Molten Salt_ with _Water_ into _Salt_ and some _Steam_ - the fast/bulk counterpart to the Solar Heater's slow evaporation trickle.
block.solarpunk.deuterium_extractor.tool: Needs Rotational Force from below to run. Pipe water in and Deuterium out of any face, or fill/drain by hand with a bucket.
Slowly extracts _Deuterium_ from _Water_ - the cheap half of the Fusion Reactor's fuel pair.
block.solarpunk.fermentation_vat.tooltip: Increases batch size and output. A 3x3 footprint processes 9 Biomass per batch. Taller vats produce super-linearly more Biofuel per batch.
Ferments _Biomass_ and water into _Biofuel_. Requires at least a _2x2 footprint_ and _4 blocks tall_ to operate.
block.solarpunk.firebox_boiler.tooltip.b: Converts water to Steam at a fixed rate. Insert fuel by hand or hopper; pipe water in and Steam out of any face.
block.solarpunk.firebox_boiler.tooltip.s: Burns furnace fuel to boil water into _Steam_ for the _Steam Turbine_. A cheap way to get a turbine running before building a Solar Power Tower - nowhere near as efficient at scale.
block.solarpunk.geyser_cap.tooltip.behav: Generates 32 RPM with 16384 SU of stress capacity. Works day and night in all weather.
block.solarpunk.geyser_cap.tooltip.condi: When placed on a Geyser Vent
block.solarpunk.geyser_cap.tooltip.summa: Harnesses the energy of a _Geyser Vent_ for passive, round-the-clock _Rotational Force_.
block.solarpunk.heat_battery.tooltip.beh: Passively heats the boiler above. Heat level fades over time.
block.solarpunk.heat_battery.tooltip.sum: Stores thermal energy as _Molten Salt_ and supplies heat to a _Boiler_ placed above it.
Charges up while _no Redstone_ signal is applied.
Discharges at 16 RPM with 256 SU of stress capacity until empty.
When connected to a spinning network
When a Redstone signal is applied
Stores _Rotational Force_ for later use. Useful for buffering intermittent generators like solar panels.
block.solarpunk.kinetic_sprinkler.toolti: Forces _instant growth_ on every crop in range each cycle.
When supplied with Fertilizer instead of water
Hydrates _farmland_ and accelerates _crop growth_ in a 5x5 area below it.
Needs Rotational Force from below to run. Insert Salt by hand, pipe water in from any face, collect Dust from the block or a hopper.

Slowly converts _Water_ and _Salt_ into _Lithium Dust_, with a small chance of _Beryllium Dust_ alongside it - a renewable floor for the Fusion Reactor's fuel chain, much slower than mining Lithium Ore.
block.solarpunk.solar_heater.tooltip.beh: Processes the loaded item. Slows in _rain_.
block.solarpunk.solar_heater.tooltip.con: During the day with a clear sky
block.solarpunk.solar_heater.tooltip.sum: Uses _sunlight_ to melt items into fluid and passively evaporate water into _Salt_.
block.solarpunk.solar_mirror.tooltip.sum: Reflects sunlight toward an adjacent _Solar Power Tower_. Over-mirroring past twice the optimal count reduces output to zero.
block.solarpunk.solar_power_tower.toolti: Output scales with tower size and mirror count. Efficiency peaks at _half_ the available wall faces covered.
Multiblock tower that concentrates reflected sunlight to produce _Molten Salt_ or _Steam_ from water. Right-click with a Wrench to switch modes.
block.solarpunk.turbine_rotor.tooltip.be: Generates power proportional to height and blade efficiency. Drains condensate water from the bottom.
block.solarpunk.turbine_rotor.tooltip.su: The power output block of the _Steam Turbine_ multiblock. Pipe _Steam_ into the casing walls and collect _Rotational Force_ from the top face.
create.solar_punk.tooltip.condensate_ful: Condensate full - drain water to restart

solarpunk.ponder.andesite_panel_usage.te: The Andesite Solar Panel generates Rotational Force from sunlight
It outputs rotation downwards - connect a shaft or machine directly below
At dawn and dusk: 8 RPM with 1024 SU of stress capacity
At noon in clear weather: 16 RPM with 4096 SU of stress capacity
Rain reduces output to dawn levels - night stops generation entirely
The panel must have a clear view of the sky directly above to function
solarpunk.ponder.biofuel_engine_usage.te: The Biofuel Engine burns Biofuel to generate Rotational Force
Pipe Biofuel into any face to fill the internal tank
With Biofuel present, it outputs 16 RPM with 8192 SU of stress capacity
Rotation exits downward - connect a shaft or machine directly below
The Biomass Gasifier burns Biomass to generate Rotational Force
Add Biomass into the top slot - each piece burns for 15 seconds
While burning, it outputs 8 RPM with 2048 SU of stress capacity
Rotation exits downward - connect a shaft or machine directly below
Output is intermittent - use a Kinetic Battery to buffer power between refills
solarpunk.ponder.brass_panel_usage.text_: The Brass Solar Panel generates Forge Energy (FE) directly from sunlight
Connect cables or conduits to any face to transfer the generated power
At dawn and dusk: 40 FE/t - at noon in clear weather: 80 FE/t
Rain reduces output to dawn levels - the panel must have clear sky access above it
solarpunk.ponder.crystallizer_usage.head: Using the Crystallizer
solarpunk.ponder.crystallizer_usage.text: The Crystallizer runs data-driven recipes: two fluids in, an item out, plus an optional fluid byproduct
By default it quenches Molten Salt with Water to produce Salt
Unlike the Solar Heater, it works day or night - cooling doesn't need sunlight
The result collects in the block's output slot - grab it by hand or pull it out with a hopper
Quenching Molten Salt also flashes off some Steam as a byproduct, ready for a Steam Turbine
solarpunk.ponder.deuterium_extractor_usa: The Deuterium Extractor slowly pulls Deuterium out of Water - the cheap half of the Fusion Reactor's fuel pair
Pipe Water into any face - unlike the Solar Heater, it needs no sunlight
Drive it with a shaft from below - it stalls without Rotational Force
Deuterium collects in its own tank - drain it from any face and pipe it to the Fusion Reactor
solarpunk.ponder.fermentation_vat_scalin: A larger footprint increases the batch size - a 2x2 vat processes 4 Biomass at once, a 3x3 processes 9
Water consumed and Biofuel produced per batch scale with the footprint area
Taller vats produce super-linearly more Biofuel per batch - the same way a taller Solar Power Tower produces more. Tank capacity also grows with each block added
Stack Fermentation Vat blocks - they merge into a single multiblock
The vat needs at least a 2x2 footprint to ferment anything
Pipe water in through any face to fill the water tank
Insert Biomass into the input from the top
The vat ferments Biomass with water into Biofuel - a 2x2 vat consumes 4 Biomass per batch
Drain Biofuel from any face and pipe it to a Biofuel Engine
solarpunk.ponder.fusion_reactor_structur: The Fusion Reactor Core sits at the exact center of a fixed spherical shell - it doesn't grow taller like the Steam Turbine, it's always this one size

Fill the inner ring band with Blanket Modules - it's an open gyroscope skeleton, not a sealed ball, so the Core stays visible through the gaps. Lithium Breeder for efficient fuel use, Beryllium Reflector for raw output, mixed in whatever ratio you want
Enclose the whole shell in Fusion Reactor Casing - swap in Casing Glass anywhere for a clear view straight through to the open Blanket band underneath
Once the shell and blanket band are complete, the reactor lights up - check it with Goggles to see its status and blanket mix
The Core itself disappears once the reactor is fully formed - all that's left floating here is the glowing rings and crackling energy
More Beryllium in the blanket burns fuel faster for more steam output; more Lithium breeds Tritium more efficiently for a lower, steadier output
Feed it with Deuterium and Lithium - a Deuterium Extractor and Lithium Brine Extractor farm keeps it running
solarpunk.ponder.geyser_cap_usage.text_1: Geyser Vents naturally generate in hot, arid biomes
solarpunk.ponder.geyser_cap_usage.text_2: Place a Geyser Cap directly on top of a Geyser Vent to harness its energy
solarpunk.ponder.geyser_cap_usage.text_3: While active, the cap generates 32 RPM with 16384 SU of stress capacity
solarpunk.ponder.geyser_cap_usage.text_4: Rotation is output along the cap's sides - connect shafts or machines to collect the power
solarpunk.ponder.heat_battery_filling.te: The Heat Battery stores thermal energy in the form of Molten Salt
Fill it by right-clicking with a Molten Salt bucket, or piping fluid into any face
Fill it to capacity for maximum heat output
The block's glow indicates heat level - brighter means hotter
solarpunk.ponder.heat_battery_usage.head: Using the Heat Battery
solarpunk.ponder.heat_battery_usage.text: A filled Heat Battery acts as a heat source for Create's steam engines
Place it directly below a Boiler to supply heat - no fuel required
The heat level depends on how much Molten Salt is stored
Stored heat dissipates slowly over time - keep it topped up with the Solar Heater
solarpunk.ponder.kinetic_battery_usage.t: The Kinetic Battery stores Rotational Force for later use
When connected to a spinning network without a Redstone signal, it charges up
Apply a Redstone signal to discharge - it outputs rotation along its axis
Discharge output: 16 RPM with 256 SU of stress capacity
The battery discharges at a constant speed until empty, then stops
Use it to buffer power from intermittent sources like solar panels
solarpunk.ponder.lithium_brine_extractor: The Lithium Brine Extractor turns Water and Salt into Lithium Dust - a slow, renewable floor for the Fusion Reactor's second fuel
Pipe Water in and feed it Salt by hand - each cycle consumes both together
Like the Deuterium Extractor, it needs a shaft driving it from below to run
Lithium Dust collects in the output slot - grab it by hand or pull it out with a hopper
Each cycle also has a small chance to produce bonus Beryllium Dust in a separate slot
It's deliberately much slower than mining Lithium Ore - a floor for when every vein nearby is stripped, not a replacement for it
solarpunk.ponder.solar_heater_evaporatio: The Solar Heater can also evaporate water into Salt
Fill the water tank by right-clicking with a water bucket, or pipe water in from the side
With sunlight present, water slowly evaporates and Salt accumulates in the second slot
Salt can be smelted into Molten Salt directly in the Solar Heater
solarpunk.ponder.solar_heater_usage.head: Using the Solar Heater
solarpunk.ponder.solar_heater_usage.text: The Solar Heater melts items into fluids using sunlight
Right-click to place an item into the input slot
During the day with clear skies, the heater slowly processes the item
The resulting fluid fills the output tank - drain it with a pipe or bucket
solarpunk.ponder.solar_power_tower_mirro: Solar Mirrors are freestanding - place them on the ground, they don't attach to the tower
A mirror links automatically if it has open sky above it and a clear line of sight to the tower
The search radius scales with the tower's height, and taller towers can track more mirrors at once
Each linked mirror's post turns to face the tower, and its plate tilts to bisect the sun and the tower - tracking the sun all day
Efficiency follows a triangle curve peaking at an optimal mirror count for the field - doubling past that drops it back to zero
Check a linked tower with Goggles to see its mirror count and current efficiency
solarpunk.ponder.solar_power_tower_usage: Stack Solar Power Tower blocks vertically - they merge into a single multiblock
The tower requires at least a 3x3 footprint and 3 blocks tall to produce anything
Pipe water in through any side face to fill the water tank
During the day with a clear sky, the tower converts water into Molten Salt - rain and night stop production
Solar Mirrors placed nearby link to the tower automatically and boost output - see the Solar Mirrors scene for details
Drain the Molten Salt from the output and pipe it to a Heat Battery
Right-click the tower with a Wrench to switch it to Steam mode - the stored fluid is cleared on switch
In Steam mode the tower produces Steam directly - pipe it to a Steam Turbine or other consumer
solarpunk.ponder.tag.bio_machines.descri: Machines for producing and burning Biofuel
solarpunk.ponder.tag.fusion_reactor.desc: Endgame direct-steam fusion power, fed by Deuterium and Lithium
solarpunk.ponder.tag.solar_machines.desc: Machines that harness the power of sunlight
solarpunk.ponder.tag.solar_tower.descrip: Concentrated solar power for producing Molten Salt
solarpunk.ponder.turbine_condensate.head: Steam Condensation
solarpunk.ponder.turbine_condensate.text: As steam drives the rotor it condenses back into water - this condensate collects inside the turbine
Check the condensate water level at any time using Engineer's Goggles on any Rotor block
When the condensate tank is full the turbine shuts down automatically - no more steam is consumed until the water is drained
Pipe the condensate water out of any casing face to drain it - the turbine restarts as soon as there is room
solarpunk.ponder.turbine_horizontal.head: Building On Its Side
solarpunk.ponder.turbine_horizontal.text: The Steam Turbine doesn't have to stand up - the same shell works lying on the East/West or North/South axis
Place the first Rotor against the face pointing the way you want it to grow - the whole structure follows that axis
It works exactly the same way from there - pipe in Steam, and power exits from the far Rotor
solarpunk.ponder.turbine_max.text_1: The sealed floor is a full 7x7 of Turbine Casing with no rotor - it anchors the structure from below
solarpunk.ponder.turbine_max.text_2: A taller turbine consumes more Steam per tick but produces proportionally more SU - height is the main throughput lever
solarpunk.ponder.turbine_max.text_3: Fill every blade slot with Brass Blades for the best Steam-to-SU efficiency
solarpunk.ponder.turbine_max.text_4: Cap the top identically to the floor - full 7x7 Casing with the Rotor at center. Power exits from the top of this rotor
solarpunk.ponder.turbine_max.text_5: Replace any casing with Turbine Casing Glass anywhere in the structure to see inside - still valid
solarpunk.ponder.turbine_max.text_6: The maximum is 20 blade layers - at full brass and max height it can power an entire base
solarpunk.ponder.turbine_structure.text_: Start with a sealed floor - fill the entire 7x7 footprint with Turbine Casing, including the center
Above the floor, build ring-only layers with a Rotor at center and Turbine Blades in the plus pattern
Two blades per arm, four arms - eight blades total per layer. Andesite is cheaper; Brass is more efficient
Stack as many blade layers as you want - each adds more throughput
Seal the top the same way as the floor - full 7x7 of Turbine Casing with the Rotor at center
Pipe Steam into any face of the outer casing wall - condensate water drains from any casing face too
Rotational power exits from the top face of the cap rotor - connect a shaft directly above
